slides.1.title: Vinho Verde DOC: A Full Introduction
slides.1.html:
"Vinho Verde" literally means "green wine", but here "green" signifies young and fresh, not colour — although most Vinho Verde is indeed white.

🗺️ Location

Located in the Minho region of northwest Portugal, right next to Galicia in Spain, a neighbour of Rías Baixas (Albariño).

🌡️ Climate

  • Atlantic climate with rainfall up to 1,500mm, the wettest region in Portugal
  • Mild, cool summers help preserve the grapes' natural acidity
  • Character: fresh, high-acid, light, with a slight natural spritz (CO₂)

🍇 Main Varieties

  • Alvarinho (white): at its best in the Monção/Melgaço sub-region
  • Loureiro (white): the main variety of the Lima sub-region
  • Trajadura (white): often used in blends
  • Vinhão (red): for dark, aromatic red Vinho Verde

📋 The 9 Sub-regions

Amarante · Ave · Baião · Basto · Cávado · Lima · Monção · Paiva · Sousa
slides.2.question: What does "Verde" (green) in the name Vinho Verde refer to?
slides.2.explanation: The "Verde" (green) in "Vinho Verde" means young and fresh, not a colour. Vinho Verde can be white, red or rosé, with white being the most common.
